Its `origin` was re-pointed at `https://github.com/LEAPWare-Software/LEAPWare-Watchtower.git` before the first session so that repo resolution and `git_hygiene` see what a stranger's clone has (a local-path remote resolves to no `owner/name`).

keys out of the chat. Both halves of each were removed on 30 July 2026 at the
owner`s instruction - the hooks that inspected commands and writes, and the six
permissions.deny groups - so both answers had stopped doing anything and the
parameters that carried them are gone too. NOTHING in this plugin refuses a
destructive command or keeps a credential out of a file or out of the chat. If
the operator asks about either, say that plainly; do not put it as a question.

  Q1  END-OF-TURN WARNINGS                                 recommended: YES
      "Shall I switch on the warnings that appear when Claude finishes a reply -
       the conversation getting close to full, work that was never checked,
       documentation left behind by a code change, uncommitted changes sitting in
       a repository? They only ever warn. They never stop anything."
      -> pass  -Advisories yes   or   -Advisories no

  Q2  THE HEALTH INDICATOR AT THE BOTTOM OF THE WINDOW     recommended: copy
      "Shall I switch on the small health indicator at the bottom of the Claude
       Code window? It turns red when something went wrong in this session.
       There are two ways to set it up:
         copy     - put a copy of the file in your home folder. Keeps working
                    even if this project folder is moved or renamed, but the copy
                    can fall behind the original and nothing tells you when it
                    has.
         junction - point at the file inside the project instead. It can never
                    fall behind, but the indicator disappears if the project
                    folder is moved, renamed, or is part-way through a git
                    operation.
         skip     - leave the bottom of the window alone."
      -> pass  -StatusLineMode copy | junction | skip

  Q3  HOW THE GOVERNANCE RUNS                              recommended: plugin
      "Claude Code has already found this plugin, so it will run its own checks
       with no further setup. Answer plugin unless you have been told otherwise:
       answering standalone would wire a SECOND copy into your settings and every
       check would then run twice."
      -> pass  -HookMode plugin | standalone

  Q4  HELPER ROLES                                         recommended: YES
      "Shall I check that the helper roles the health indicator depends on are
       present? This only looks and reports - it writes nothing at all."
      -> pass  -AgentRoles yes   or   -AgentRoles no

THEN, ONE SECTION AT A TIME AND ONE YES EACH:
  1. -Step diff -Section statusline    then apply, only if the operator agrees
  2. -Step diff -Section hooks         then apply, only if the operator agrees
  3. -Step doctor

A no to any one section leaves that section untouched and does not cancel the
others. Every apply is preceded by its own diff and its own yes. Add -DryRun to
an apply to do everything except the write.

    between - and the CLI rewrites it itself - the write is refused.)

statusLine is a settings.json key. A plugin cannot supply one - there is no
manifest field for it and no hook event renders a line - which is half the reason
this installer exists. It renders the HH health segment, and it is this plugin's
only CONTINUOUS indicator - not its only visible one. Unwired, you still get the
banner at session start and an advisory at the end of a turn; what you lose is
everything in between, which is where a fault first shows.

--- WHAT WOULD CHANGE -----------------------------------------------------
MODE: copy
  A copy of the tracked file goes into your home folder, and the setting points at
  the copy.
  TRADE-OFF: the indicator keeps working if this project folder is moved, renamed,
  or is part-way through a git operation. But the copy and the original are then
  two independent files and NOTHING on this machine compares them automatically -
  edit either and the other is silently stale, including the case that costs most,
  a fix made to the live copy and overwritten the next time this is run.
  /lw-watchtower:doctor is what detects that drift, afterwards.

  ACTION 1  create
            file  C:\kstmp\uat-cpo-step5\profile\statusline.ps1
            from  C:\kstmp\uat-cpo-step5\profile\plugins\cache\leapware-watchtower\lw-watchtower\0.4.0\statusline\statusline.ps1

  ACTION 2  set the statusLine key in the settings file

  BEFORE:
    (not set)
  AFTER:
    {
        "type":  "command",
        "command":  "powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File \"C:/kstmp/uat-cpo-step5/profile/statusline.ps1\"",
        "refreshInterval":  120
    }

--- WHAT WOULD NOT CHANGE -------------------------------------------------
  2 other top-level key(s) compared value-by-value: all unchanged
  No other section is touched. statusLine and hooks are written
  one at a time, each behind its own yes.

FORMATTING NOTE, so it is not a surprise afterwards: applying re-serialises the
whole file. Indentation becomes PowerShell's four spaces, and the characters
< > & ' are written as \u003c \u003e \u0026 \u0027. Every VALUE is unchanged and
the file is backed up first, but the byte layout of untouched sections does move.

TO APPLY (2 change(s)), and ONLY if the operator has said yes to THIS section:

  ... -File bin\lwg-setup.ps1 -Step apply -Section statusline -BaseHash d8977d3f1a8b2a2a12b2822cb6e16a180c52c0e2a9e39c43cf674128798ea5ab -Advisories yes -AgentRoles yes -HookMode auto -StatusLineMode copy

  Add -DryRun to that line to do everything except the write.

#### 8b — `bin\lwg-toggle.ps1 -Flag delegate` (report only; never `on` — an armed gate persists in the state directory) — exit 0

<details><summary>whole output</summary>

```
delegate is OFF    (reserve the chat session for operator communication - all work goes to subagents)

  changed        : nothing was written - no value was given, so this is a report only
  global default : off
  repo override  : none - falls through to the global default   [LEAPWare-Software/LEAPWare-Watchtower]
  effective here : OFF
  stored in      : C:\kstmp\uat-cpo-step5\profile\plugins\data\lw-watchtower-leapware-watchtower\config.override.json -> interaction.delegate
  merged over    : C:\kstmp\uat-cpo-step5\profile\plugins\cache\leapware-watchtower\lw-watchtower\0.4.0\config.json   [the shipped defaults; this command never writes it]
  config source  : config.json
  override       : none yet - every value above is the shipped default

IN EFFECT FROM NOW ON, in this session:

  Work may be done directly on the main thread.

ENFORCED - what this switch actually blocks, and what that costs

  delegate IS enforced, and it is the only thing in this plugin that is. Turning it on
  arms delegate_gate - lib/gate_delegate.ps1, a PreToolUse hook on
  Edit|Write|NotebookEdit|Bash|PowerShell - which REFUSES those five tools for any call that did
  not come from a subagent. The refusal is a real block: PreToolUse deny is honoured
  even under permissions.defaultMode "bypassPermissions". A subagent is identified by
  the presence of agent_id in the hook payload, never by agent_type, because a
  settings.json `agent` key gives the MAIN thread a non-empty agent_type.
  
  WHAT TURNING IT ON COSTS, and it is not reversible from here: with the gate armed,
  /lw-watchtower:delegate off will NOT work from the main thread. This command runs through
  Bash, and Bash is one of the five tools refused - so is PowerShell, so switching shell
  is not a way round it either. There is deliberately no exemption
  for it - an exemption for "the command that turns me off" is a named bypass. The two
  ways back are to have a SUBAGENT run /lw-watchtower:delegate off, or to set
  interaction.delegate to false by hand in the override file named under `stored in`
  above - config.json in the plugin root is the shipped defaults and setting it there
  would be overridden by the file that says true.
  
  What it still does NOT do: it does not check that a dispatch was any good, and it
  refuses nothing a subagent does. Delegation is enforced; delegating well is not.

  A governance module. delegate is the switch on delegate_gate in the module
  registry in lib/common.ps1 - kind "gate", the only one - so the banner counts it
  and the live-gate count moves with it. Its FLAG stays out of the "modules" block
  on purpose: one gate must have one switch, and Get-LwgConfig fails OPEN, which
  would arm a blocking hook off an unreadable config. The SessionStart banner
  reports gates shipped and gates live as separate numbers; start a new session,
  or read interaction.delegate in C:\kstmp\uat-cpo-step5\profile\plugins\data\lw-watchtower-leapware-watchtower\config.override.json, to see this land.
```

## The pages, judged as a reader

**`README.md`** at `1baf6d4`, as a stranger's only page: the two install lines work as written and now tell you which commit you got (and they were right — `1baf6d4`, three ways). The doctor step tells you what the `1` means before you see it and what to run next, and "the whole install" now comes after that step rather than before it. The update row says what happens on the route the page recommends. Nothing on the page turned out false in this pass.

**`docs/install.md`** told the truth about everything I saw: the two trees, the commit commands, the setup mechanics, the exit-code paragraph, the `Get-FileHash` note, the PowerShell 7 condition, and — the part that was worst last time — the whole uninstall sequence on the marketplace route, both forms, including the `.orphaned_at` marker and what not to read into it. The one thing it cannot fix is that the command it sends you to (`/lw-watchtower:uninstall`) still contradicts it on the state directory.

**`SUPPORT.md`**: one route per kind, every link 200, blank issues disabled as it says, the five-day promise stated as a reply and not a fix. Nothing to file.

## Step count

28 steps: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4a, 4b, 5a, 5b (stopped), 6a, 6b, 6c, 6d, 6e, 6f, 7, 8a, 8b, 8c, 8d, 9 (stopped), 10, 11a, 11b, 11c, 11d, 12, 13, S (step 0 is the BEFORE hash and step 13 the AFTER). Two of them were live `claude -p` sessions, both unauthenticated (the placed credential could not be refreshed); zero authenticated sessions ran, and no credential was read, copied, hashed or captured.

## Verdict

I would ship this to a stranger today with one caveat named on the box: every one of the nine things that stopped the last stranger is fixed or truthfully documented at `1baf6d4` — the install, the doctor's first verdict, the PowerShell 7 launch, the commit question, the update row, the uninstall page — and the only thing I measured that still lies to an operator is the uninstaller's own `kept - this is evidence` line on the marketplace route, which sends them to the command that deletes it (#280, script half); that is the single worst thing I saw, and it is a sentence, not a mechanism. What this pass could not do is watch the six slash commands run live, so the #277 refusal count — the one number a live session was placed here to measure — is still unmeasured.
